links.outcome: Change in LLM smoking-cessation fact coverage across user personas varying age, expertise, smoking history
links.effect: Every model named FDA-approved prescription cessation medications less often to teen than adult personas, by 32 to 67 percentage points; five of six models gave fewer facts to a persona presenting healthcare expertise.
links.quote: Every model named FDA-approved prescription cessation medications less often to teen personas than to adult personas, by 32 to 67 percentage points, and in five of six models a persona presenting health- care expertise received fewer facts than a persona presenting none.

links.outcome: Consistency of LLM responses across personas that differ in life stage, expertise, and smoking history
links.effect: Responses varied by persona: teen personas received prescription medication mentions 32 to 67 percentage points less often than adults; expert personas received fewer facts in five of six models.
links.quote: What the models say depends on who appears to be asking.

unlisted_practices: System prompt specifying a factual floor of core medical facts for all users, which narrowed persona differences in every model but had variable effects on overall fact coverage across models

links.effect: Across six LLMs, the prompt narrowed persona differences in every model, but overall fact coverage varied in magnitude and direction.
links.quote: The prompt narrows persona differences in every model, but its effect on overall fact coverage varies in both magnitude and direction across models, so a prompt validated on one system cannot be assumed to transfer to another.
